Visit note | 2026-01-06 04:00 PM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Sharmin Bhuiyan, 28, female. Ms. Bhuiyan attends for her first visit complaining of painful cramps during the first days of each menstrual period, accompanied by nausea, which frequently forces her to miss work or classes. She works as a tailor, and notes her symptoms have grown much worse since taking on a job requiring long standing hours in Kushtia. She reports no other systemic illness and has no known comorbidities. On examination: pain score 7/10, BP 111/78 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 90 kg. Abdominal examination is soft with mild tenderness in the lower quadrants and no guarding. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: a prescription was issued for symptom relief. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, engage in light exercise, and keep a detailed period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.

Visit note | 2026-01-06 04:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Popy Awal, 78, female. Mrs. Awal returns for review, reporting a burning sensation behind her breastbone after meals, an unpleasant sour taste in her mouth, and symptoms that become noticeably worse when she lies down. She works as a homemaker and mentions her discomfort worsened after weeks of eating fried snacks at local tea stalls in Cox's Bazar. She denies dysphagia or unintended weight loss and has no chronic comorbidities. On examination: BMI 28.1, BP 117/86 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 72 kg. Abdominal palpation reveals mild epigastric tenderness without masses. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: a prescription was issued to control acid production. She was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of her bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2026-01-06 04:30 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Sajjad Ahmed, 21, male. Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.
